principles.text: Holds a losing position overnight as long as it has not hit his stop; about 95% of the time he will not take it off manually.

If a stock gaps below his stop, about 95% of the time he sells at the open and lets the stop trigger rather than waiting for a bounce; he can buy back on a 1-minute opening-range-high breakout if the stock reacts positively after stopping him out.
Rarely sizes above 25% of the account in high-ADR stocks unless he has really high conviction in that trade idea.

Calculates position size from his original account size rather than the grown one (e.g. 10K, not 13K after a 30% run), so he sizes up slowly and has a buffer that avoids having to size down in a mild drawdown.
Position-size percentages are computed on pure account equity, never including margin buying power; sizing off 3x buying power risks blow-up on a ~33% drawdown.
Shorting gold and silver is not a valid reason to short copper.
Avoids stacking more exposure on the same theme (skipped a DUST long while already short gold) so as not to be greedy into a possible ugly gap the next day.

Big returns in a reversal rally come from being fully prepared for the turn so he can size up and build exposure across multiple positions quickly; tight stops with a low win rate increase the upside.
Win rate is an output of his trading, not an input; focus on the inputs, i.e. entries and timing.
Self-assessment: his selling is much poorer than his entries; he exits longs too early out of fear of giving back gains when a stock gets extended.
To shrink a focus list, raise the volatility and liquidity criteria and favour faster, more liquid, higher-priced names: easier to trade, less slippage, lower trading cost.
Spends most study effort journaling and reviewing his own trades, especially losses, one by one (entry, exit, what went wrong vs the market) and looking for commonalities in losing trades.
Losses taken while sizing up during a losing streak are far larger than normal losses; simply not sizing up in a losing streak prevents them, and confronting the figures is what fixed it.
